messages:
ashok: Heads up — release cut is blocked. Staging CI runners are piling up and the cache layer is returning 429/slow responses, which is causing the smoke tests to OOM and fail the job. deploy-bot is stuck in "promotion_pending state."

deploy-bot: promotion blocked: CI_PIPELINE_FAILURE (staging-smoke), reason=cache_backpressure (read 429s). Manual intervention required.

maria: can you paste the failing log lines?

ashok: logs from the failing smoke job (trimmed):
```
E 03:42:11 runner.cache: read(key=prefix/kv/12345) -> 429 TooManyRequests
W 03:42:12 test.runner: allocating heap 1.6GB -> killed by OOM
E 03:42:12 pytest: received non-zero exit 137 for test_flow::smoke
```

olivia: looks like multiple runners are hitting the same cache store and it's rate-limiting. Could be our redis proxy around the artifact cache.

sam: is this only staging? any sign of the same in prod-runner metrics?

ashok: only staging so far. redis-proxy metrics show connection queue spike and 5xx/429 bursts around 03:40-03:45.

maria: quick mitigations: 1) re-run smoke with CACHE=off 2) purge stale cache entries for the commit range 3) increase runner memory for this job. Which do we want to try first?

eng-oncall: I'd prefer a minimally-invasive approach: try re-run with CACHE=off for one job to unblock the promote decision, while we investigate the proxy. If the re-run passes, we can manual-promote the image and continue the release window.

olivia: +1. Also create an incident for the cache proxy so infra is aware (paging infra team).

ashok: ok I'll kick a smoke job with CACHE=off now and open a cache proxy incident. If that passes, we pin to last-green and manually promote.

ashok: kicked job: #staging-smoke/1723 (no-cache) — re-run started.

deploy-bot: note: manual-promote requires 2 approvers when canary is skipped per release-policy.

sam: I can approve manual promote if smoke passes. maria can you be second?

maria: yes I can approve.

olivia: incident created: INC-2023-cache-proxy-backpressure, paging infra oncall. Link: https://pagerduty/INC-2023-cache-proxy-backpressure

ashok: re-run passed: smoke job exited 0. Looks good.

sam: approving manual promote now.

maria: approving as well.

deploy-bot: manual promote triggered by @sam and @maria. Promoting image sha: sha256:abcdef123456 -> release/cut/2026-03-21.

ashok: two operational notes: 1) I'm opening a follow-up PR to pin the release to this sha in the release manifest (so we don't accidentally roll forward), 2) we should add a short blurb to release notes about "temporary cache bypass" for staging validation.

olivia: agreed on the PR. Also we should schedule a postmortem and consider adding retry/backoff and circuit-breaker on the cache proxy for runners.

sam: I'll add a TODO to the rollout checklist: if cache_proxy_error_rate > 5% during staging, try no-cache re-run then escalate.

ashok: PR opened: https://git/release-manifests/pin-2026-03-21 (links to sha). I'll also attach the smoke job logs.

eng-oncall: marking release as promoted manually. We'll leave canary in place for 30m observation, but the cut is unblocked. Please coordinate with infra for the cache fix.

olivia: infra is on it — they reported a misconfigured connection pool on the redis-proxy that caused a backpressure loop. Hotfix rolling now.

ashok: thanks everyone. Follow-up actions: (1) infra to complete hotfix and confirm proxy metrics normalized (2) eng to merge pin PR (3) ops to file postmortem. I'll update release notes and close this thread when done.

sam: closing in favor of tracked tasks. Great rapid coordination. :thumbsup:
